items.fact: The campaign is split into five chapters, and PC Gamer counts 91 story missions in its mission list.

Game Rant lists five chapters and 92 main story missions, with a story playtime of 65 to 70 hours. Its per-chapter counts are 22, 11, 26, 25 and 7. Outlets differ on the mission total: PC Gamer says 91 and VGC says 95.

Lucia is released from prison in the Chapter 1 mission Coming Home. You can only explore as her in free roam from the start of Chapter 2, and free switching between her and Jason unlocks after the mission Coffee Break.

Tourist Trap is Chapter 1's point of no return. Starting it kicks off a run of connected missions that stops you roaming as both leads for several hours. You also lose access to Jason's Ultimate Edition vehicles.
Chapter 3 moves Jason and Lucia to Vice City. There they work for Dre'Quan Priest, Boobie Ike and Raul Bautista, and you can freely switch between the two leads.
Rockstar has posted a full high-resolution map of Vice City and the wider Leonida state. The map is covered in fog of war until you explore it.
Leonida has five counties. Named areas include Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga National Park.
There are 18 collectible card sets spread across Leonida's counties. Each set has its own card total, for example 24 cards in the Vice City Flamingos set and 36 in Jack of Hearts.
Collecting three cards in each of the five counties unlocks the Collectible Cards achievement. Cards sell for varying amounts, so a rare one can bring in thousands.
There are 125 Cocaine Flamingos to find. Each must be destroyed to count, and the drugs inside can be sold.
Doubloons found by diving off Leonida's coast can be sold to Kenton in Key Lento for a profit.
Side activities include racing (street, sea and off-road), the gym, hunting, fishing, base jumping, clubbing, billiards, mini golf and a shooting range.
The biggest payouts come from large bank vault robberies, worth up to $200,000 each and unlocked near the end of Chapter 4. Randy's high-end car orders from Chapter 3 pay $30,000 or more per car.
Gang hideouts show yellow map icons with the gang, security level and possible score. Selling the loot to dealers pays almost immediately.
Cars with trackers can't be sold to Moses, who buys stolen cars from Chapter 2. Moses pays roughly $1,000 to $5,000 per car, and sleeping at a safehouse resets his sales cooldown.
After Island Dreams in Chapter 1, Kenton in Key Lento unlocks sunken-treasure dives. Hauls sell for up to about $2,600 each.
Randy has a wish list of 18 high-end sports cars. Moses and Randy give you tools for stealing vehicles, and Randy's include key cloning for modern cars.
Bank and loan-store robberies need a dye pack jammer, which you only get from a Chapter 3 contact. Robbing medium- or high-security places is much easier with a partner.
Buses and trains work as fast travel across the world. They run on schedules, so you have to wait for them to arrive.
Coming Home is timed, and you need to reach the prison around 2:10pm. If you are late, Lucia takes the bus and your relationship takes a serious hit.

The optional pre-release errands in Chapter 1 boost the Jason and Lucia relationship, but they disappear once you pick Lucia up. They include fixing the house and car and buying flowers and a necklace.

Update 1.002.002 went out on November 23 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It fixes crashes, autosaves failing, weather that never changed, missing story phone calls and being unable to lose a wanted level. It also fixes the gym deadlift bar and partners not handing over bags to sell to fences.
Because of the autosave bug, players have been advised to save manually. The first patch download is about 604 MB on PS5 and 1.6 GB on Xbox.
The first patch doesn't mention the glitch that forces a first-person view, nor the Xbox glitch that unlocks 60fps.
